definition: Relating to the legal process of asking a higher court to change a decision.

collocations.example: The appellate court reviewed the case and reduced the original fine.
An appellate judge reads the written arguments before making a final ruling.

definition: An underground layer of rock or sand that holds water and lets it be pumped out.

collocations.example: The town pumps its drinking water from a deep underground aquifer.
Heavy farming can slowly drain the aquifer that supplies nearby farms.

definition: Describing land that is suitable for growing crops.

collocations.example: Much of the region's arable land is now used to grow wheat.
Arable farming depends on good soil, steady rain, and warm weather.

definition: A person or group with the power to settle a dispute or decide what is right.

collocations.example: The courts are the final arbiter of what the new law really means.
For years the magazine was seen as the arbiter of taste in fashion.

definition: A long solo song for one voice in an opera or other large musical work.

collocations.example: The soprano stepped forward to sing a famous aria from the opera.
The concert opened with a beautiful aria that silenced the whole audience.

definition: Weapons and military equipment used by an army, ship, or country.

collocations.example: The warship carried heavy armament designed for long battles at sea.
The country's armament industry supplies weapons to several foreign governments.

definition: The hollow area under your arm where it joins your shoulder.

collocations.example: The nurse placed the thermometer under the armpit to take his temperature.
Warm weather can make armpit hair feel damp and uncomfortable.

definition: Money that is owed and should already have been paid.

collocations.example: They fell two months in arrears with the rent after losing the job.
The family promised to pay off the arrears over the next five years.

definition: A chemical element that is a strong poison, found in some minerals and water.

collocations.example: Tests found traces of arsenic in the old factory's drinking water.
The doctor suspected arsenic poisoning after studying the patient's symptoms.

definition: Clever and skillful at getting what you want, sometimes in a slightly cunning way.

collocations.example: Her artful move in the meeting won support without seeming pushy.
He is an artful negotiator who always finds a clever compromise.

definition: A round green vegetable with thick leaves that are cooked and eaten.

collocations.example: She boiled a fresh artichoke and served it with melted butter.
The salad was topped with soft artichoke hearts and olive oil.

definition: A long, thin green vegetable with a soft tip, eaten cooked.

collocations.example: He grilled fresh asparagus and served it beside the roasted chicken.
She bought a bunch of asparagus at the market for dinner.

definition: A black, sticky substance mixed with stones to make road surfaces.

collocations.example: Workers arrived early to lay fresh asphalt on the damaged road.
The new asphalt road was smooth and quiet to drive on.

definition: To do something to show you are sorry for a wrong or mistake.

collocations.example: He worked for free to atone for the harm his mistake had caused.
He could never fully atone for the pain he had caused.

definition: A large open space with a high roof in the middle of a building.

collocations.example: The hotel's glass atrium let sunlight fall onto the plants below.
Visitors gathered in the central atrium before the tour began.

definition: The slow reduction in the number of employees as people leave and are not replaced.

collocations.example: The company's high attrition rate meant it was always hiring new staff.
Better pay and benefits helped reduce staff attrition last year.

definition: To make someone or something able to understand or deal well with a situation.

collocations.example: Good managers stay attuned to the needs and moods of their team.
It took time to attune yourself to the fast pace of the new office.

definition: Not usual or normal; different from the typical case.

collocations.example: The doctor noted that this was an atypical case with unusual symptoms.
Her sudden silence was atypical behavior for such a talkative person.

definition: A green fruit with a large seed and soft flesh, eaten in salads and dips.

collocations.example: She mashed a ripe avocado and spread it on warm toast.
He cooked the fish in avocado oil for a mild, rich flavor.

definition: Having far too much of something, usually money or supplies.

collocations.example: After the deal, the company was awash with cash and eager to expand.
The local shops are awash with imports that undercut domestic prices.

definition: For a short period of time.

collocations.example: Please wait awhile and the manager will see you shortly.
They asked the guests to stay awhile and enjoy more coffee.

definition: A statement that most people accept as clearly true.

collocations.example: It is an old axiom that a happy customer brings more business.
A basic axiom of good service is to listen before you speak.

definition: A large amount of work that has not yet been done and is waiting.

collocations.example: After the holidays, she faced a huge backlog of work and emails.
Extra staff were hired to clear the backlog of unprocessed orders.

definition: An officer who keeps order in a court and assists the judge.

collocations.example: The court bailiff asked everyone to stand as the judge entered.
The bailiff swore in each witness before the trial began.

definition: A popular activity or trend that more and more people join.

collocations.example: Once sales rose, rival firms rushed to jump on the bandwagon.
He joined the political bandwagon only after it became popular.

definition: The rail along the side of a staircase that you hold for support.

collocations.example: She held the banister tightly as she walked down the steep stairs.
The children loved to slide down the banister when no one was watching.

definition: Friendly, playful conversation with jokes and light teasing.

collocations.example: He enjoyed exchanging banter with the customers at the front desk.
The meeting began with some good-natured banter about the weekend game.

definition: Extremely cruel and violent.

collocations.example: People across the country condemned the barbaric act of violence.
The report described the barbaric treatment of the prisoners.

definition: A poet, especially one from long ago who wrote or recited poems.

collocations.example: The ancient bard sang long poems about heroes and famous battles.
A wandering bard traveled from town to town, telling stories in verse.

definition: Something that shows changes in a situation or the state of something.

collocations.example: House prices are often a barometer of the wider economy.
Infant health is a reliable barometer of a country's living conditions.

definition: A lawyer who is qualified to argue cases in the higher courts.

collocations.example: She practiced as a barrister for many years before becoming a judge.
The defense barrister questioned the witness carefully in court.

definition: A large, important church with a long central hall.

collocations.example: Tourists lined up to visit the ancient basilica in the old city.
Visitors gazed up at the basilica's huge painted dome.

definition: A person, place, or group that strongly defends a belief or way of life.

collocations.example: The small college was seen as the last bastion of old teaching methods.
The club long remained a bastion of tradition and formal dress.

definition: The basic ideas or facts on which something is built.

collocations.example: Trust is the bedrock of any strong business relationship.
These simple rules form the bedrock of the company's culture.

definition: To happen to someone, especially something bad.

collocations.example: They worried about the troubles that might befall them on the trip.
Whatever misfortune befalls us, the family always stays together.

definition: To become a friend to someone, especially someone who needs help.

collocations.example: She was kind enough to befriend a stranger who seemed lost and alone.
The teacher asked the class to befriend the newcomer from another country.

definition: To let out gas from your stomach noisily through your mouth.

collocations.example: He finished his drink and belched loudly at the table.
She covered her mouth and tried not to belch during the meeting.

definition: To officially leave your property to someone after you die.

collocations.example: She chose to bequeath her house to her youngest daughter.
The old man decided to bequeath a small fortune to the local hospital.

definition: Money or property that someone leaves to others in their will.

collocations.example: He left a generous bequest to each of his grandchildren.
The museum was saved by a large charitable bequest from a private donor.

definition: A soft, round, flat cap with no brim.

collocations.example: He liked to wear a beret and dark glasses around town.
The soldier's black beret marked him as a member of a special unit.

definition: Romantically or sexually attracted to both men and women.

collocations.example: The actor spoke to the press as an openly bisexual man.
She has several bisexual friends who are open about their relationships.

definition: To make a very loud, harsh, unpleasant sound.

collocations.example: The music blared from the car as it sped down the street.
Loudspeakers began to blare out warnings across the crowded square.

definition: A small mark or fault that spoils the appearance or quality of something.

collocations.example: A small blemish on her skin faded after about a week.
After careful checking, the new car was sold without a single blemish.

definition: A small, round lump or drop of something soft or sticky.

collocations.example: You only need a small blob of glue to fix the broken handle.
A blob of paint fell from the brush onto the clean floor.

definition: Loud, angry, or boastful talk that has little real meaning or effect.

collocations.example: I wasn't frightened by his threats; it was all bluster.
His speech was full of bluster but offered no real solutions.

definition: To shout to show that you strongly dislike a person or performance.

collocations.example: The crowd began to boo loudly when the referee made the call.
The angry audience tried to boo the singer off the stage.

definition: Valuable goods taken by force, especially during a war or by thieves.

collocations.example: The soldiers carried home works of art as war booty.
The pirates agreed to share the booty equally among the crew.

definition: Very close to the line between two conditions, so hard to judge.

collocations.example: In borderline cases, teachers make the final decision about the grade.
His test score was a borderline pass, just above the limit.

definition: A main branch of a tree.

collocations.example: She rested the lantern against a low pine bough.
A heavy bough broke off during the storm and blocked the path.

definition: A wide city street, often with trees along both sides.

collocations.example: They strolled along a tree-lined boulevard on a warm summer evening.
The hotel stands on a busy boulevard near the city center.

definition: A type of American whiskey made mainly from corn.

collocations.example: He poured himself a glass of bourbon after the long day.
They sat on the porch to sip bourbon and watch the sunset.

definition: To talk too proudly about what you have or have done.

collocations.example: He likes to brag about his success, which annoys his coworkers.
She would often brag that her team was the best in the company.

definition: A system of raised dots that blind people read by touch.

collocations.example: The museum offers guidebooks printed in braille for blind visitors.
She learned to read braille quickly after losing her sight.

definition: The outer covering of grain, removed when making white flour.

collocations.example: He adds wheat bran to his cereal for extra fiber.
She ate a bowl of bran flakes with milk every morning.

definition: To wave something, especially a weapon, in a threatening or excited way.

collocations.example: The robber began to brandish a weapon and shouted at the staff.
The actor brandished a sword as he ran across the stage.

definition: A child who behaves badly and is rude or spoiled.

collocations.example: He acted like a spoiled brat whenever he did not get his way.
The little brat kicked the seat in front of him all through the flight.

definition: A word you shout to praise a good performance.

collocations.example: The audience stood to shout bravo as the singer finished.
Fans began to cry bravo when the final goal was scored.

definition: Behaving in a bold, shameless way without caring what others think.

collocations.example: He told a brazen lie to his boss without any sign of guilt.
It was a brazen attempt to steal credit for someone else's work.

definition: The position of a baby that is going to be born bottom or feet first.

collocations.example: A breech birth can be risky, so doctors watch the mother closely.
The baby was in a breech position, so a Cesarean was planned.

definition: Fellow members of a group, religion, or community.

collocations.example: We must do all we can to help our weaker brethren.
He urged his fellow brethren to stay united in difficult times.

definition: Water with a lot of salt in it, used for preserving food.

collocations.example: Soak the meat in brine overnight to make it tender and tasty.
The olives are stored in a salty brine until they are ready to eat.

definition: To mention a subject for the first time, especially a difficult one.

collocations.example: She was nervous about how to broach the subject of money with him.
He waited for a calm moment to broach the question of pay.

definition: A piece of jewelry pinned to clothing for decoration.

collocations.example: She wore a diamond brooch on the collar of her coat.
He gave his mother a silver brooch for her birthday.

definition: The main force or worst part of something bad.

collocations.example: Young workers often bear the brunt of job cuts during a recession.
Coastal towns took the brunt of the powerful storm.

definition: A short, strong dog with a large head and a flat face.

collocations.example: They adopted a French bulldog with short legs and a wrinkled face.
An English bulldog can overheat quickly in very hot weather.

definition: Large, strong, and heavily built (used about a person).

collocations.example: A big, burly man stood guard at the entrance to the club.
A burly figure in a dark coat blocked the narrow doorway.

definition: A way of speaking with a soft, rolling 'r' sound, typical of some regions.

collocations.example: She spoke with a soft West Country burr that charmed everyone.
His gentle Scottish burr made the story even more pleasant to hear.

definition: To laugh in a loud, harsh, unpleasant way.

collocations.example: The old woman began to cackle with laughter at the joke.
They cackled loudly at the back of the room during the show.

definition: A soft, poisonous metal used in batteries and some paints.

collocations.example: Workers at the old plant were tested for signs of cadmium poisoning.
Inspectors found traces of cadmium in the cheap toy's paint.

definition: A very serious event that causes great harm or suffering.

collocations.example: The flood was a terrible calamity that destroyed hundreds of homes.
The village was slowly rebuilt after the natural calamity.

definition: A branch of advanced mathematics that studies change and motion.

collocations.example: She had to study calculus in her first year of engineering.
Newton developed ideas that are fundamental to modern calculus.

definition: Not caring about other people's feelings or suffering.

collocations.example: His callous remark about the layoffs upset the whole office.
The manager's callous attitude toward sick staff angered everyone.

definition: A metal or plastic container with a lid, used for storing things.

collocations.example: She kept the flour in a metal canister on the kitchen shelf.
He changed the gas canister before lighting the camping stove.

definition: A drug made from the hemp plant, illegal in many countries.

collocations.example: He was arrested for possession of cannabis near the station.
Police suspected that someone had been smoking cannabis in the building.

definition: Accepted as official, standard, or authoritative.

collocations.example: Scholars still argue about which books belong in the canonical text.
The team agreed to treat this file as the canonical version of the report.

definition: A risky or daring scheme, often one that is illegal.

collocations.example: Their little caper to smuggle the jewels almost worked perfectly.
The film follows a gang planning a daring caper at a bank.

definition: A very thin blood vessel that connects arteries and veins.

collocations.example: Oxygen passes from a tiny capillary into the surrounding tissue.
The thin capillary wall lets nutrients reach the cells.

definition: To stop resisting and agree to what someone else wants; to surrender.

collocations.example: They were finally forced to capitulate to the workers' demands.
Despite the pressure, the small firm refused to capitulate.

definition: A person who holds someone else as a prisoner.

collocations.example: The hostage slowly began to trust his captor over the long weeks.
She managed to escape from her captors during the night.

definition: A sweet, sticky brown food made by heating sugar.

collocations.example: She ordered an ice cream covered in warm salted caramel.
He poured thick caramel sauce over the warm apple pie.

definition: A knitted sweater that opens at the front with buttons.

collocations.example: She put on a warm woolen cardigan before going outside.
He wore a red cardigan over his white shirt to the party.

definition: The violent killing of a large number of people.

collocations.example: Rescue teams were shocked by the terrible carnage at the scene.
The battlefield was a scene of carnage that no one could forget.

definition: A shelter for a car, with a roof but usually open at the sides.

collocations.example: She parked the car under the carport to keep it out of the rain.
They decided to build a carport beside the house for the new van.

definition: A strong, flexible tissue in the body, found in the nose, ears, and joints.

collocations.example: The athlete had to rest after he tore a cartilage in his knee.
The soft cartilage in a baby's nose slowly becomes firmer with age.

definition: To remove the testicles of a male animal or person.

collocations.example: Farmers often castrate young male animals to make them calmer.
The vet advised them to castrate the dog while it was still young.

definition: A set of fixed questions and answers used to teach religious beliefs.

collocations.example: The children had to learn the catechism before their first ceremony.
The priest used a short catechism to teach the main points of the faith.

definition: A thin tube put into the body to add or remove fluid.

collocations.example: The nurse carefully inserted a catheter to drain the fluid.
The patient needed a urinary catheter after the operation.

definition: A long raised platform that models walk along in a fashion show.

collocations.example: The models walked slowly down the catwalk in the latest designs.
The new collection was revealed at a glamorous catwalk show.

definition: Using cruel, bitter humor or criticism to hurt someone.

collocations.example: His caustic remarks about her work left everyone uncomfortable.
The critic was famous for his sharp and caustic wit.

definition: A warning that limits or explains a statement or agreement.

collocations.example: The deal was good, with one caveat: payment had to be made in cash.
The report praised the plan but added a caveat about rising costs.

definition: To give up power, land, or rights, often unwillingly.

collocations.example: The founder was reluctant to cede control of the company he built.
The defeated nation was forced to cede territory to its neighbor.

definition: The 100th anniversary of an important event.

collocations.example: The club will celebrate its centenary with a special dinner next year.
Thousands joined the centenary celebrations in the town square.

definition: The stopping of an activity or process.

collocations.example: Both sides finally agreed to an immediate cessation of hostilities.
Doctors recommend a complete cessation of smoking for faster recovery.

definition: A very deep crack or opening in the ground.

collocations.example: A deep chasm opened in the rock after the earthquake.
A narrow wooden bridge stretched across the chasm.

definition: Slightly rude or disrespectful, but in a playful, amusing way.

collocations.example: He gave a cheeky grin after making the joke about his boss.
The cheeky child stuck out his tongue and ran away laughing.

definition: To scold or criticize someone gently for doing something wrong.

collocations.example: She began to chide him for arriving late to the meeting again.
The teacher would gently chide students who forgot their homework.

definition: To make the short, high sound of a small bird or insect.

collocations.example: At dawn the birds began to chirp loudly outside the window.
The little sparrow chirped happily from the top of the fence.

definition: Polite and honorable behavior, especially by men toward women.

collocations.example: Holding the door open for her was a small act of chivalry.
Tales of brave knights come from the age of chivalry long ago.

definition: A close friend.

collocations.example: He met an old chum from school at the train station.
She invited her best chum to join the family holiday.
